claims.text: A controlled slower thermal treatment increases atomic diffusion in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
A controlled slower thermal treatment enhances homogeneous nucleation in these nanoparticles.
Increased diffusion and homogeneous nucleation suppress phase separation and elemental segregation.
Slower thermal treatment promotes a stable single-phase FCC solid solution.
Rapid heating and cooling often produce phase separation, elemental segregation, and nonuniform morphology in noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles.
The intervention consists of moderate heating rates, an elevated-temperature annealing hold, and subsequent cooling.
An elevated-temperature annealing hold provides sufficient time for atomic diffusion before final cooling.
The proposed intervention applies to nearly equiatomic nanoparticles containing more than five noble metal elements.
Enhanced diffusion reduces local compositional fluctuations and mitigates kinetic trapping.
The slower thermal profile supplies enough time and thermal energy for atoms to overcome kinetic barriers.
Overcoming kinetic barriers permits more uniform atomic diffusion and mixing.
The thermodynamically favored configuration of the targeted systems is single-phase FCC rather than a metastable phase-segregated or multiphase state.
Relative to rapid heating and cooling, slower treatment will increase the amount and uniformity of single-phase FCC material and reduce elemental segregation and secondary phases.
Rapid synthesis regimes lead to nonuniform crystal structures and irregular particle morphology.
The effect of the thermal intervention may depend on nanoparticle size and the specific elemental combination.
The optimal temperature, heating rate, and hold time are undetermined and may vary with particle size and elemental interactions.
The proposed test compares composition- and precursor-matched rapid-treatment and slow-treatment samples.

The hypothesis is falsified if slower-treated samples show no statistically significant increase in uniform single-phase FCC structure and no corresponding reduction in phase separation or segregation.
